portfolio_turnover.text:
`transaction_cost_analysis` asks what your trades cost: it compares each fill's executed price with an arrival or VWAP benchmark and reports quantity-weighted slippage in basis points. With `decision_price` it can also add delay cost and implementation shortfall, and with `unexecuted_quantity` and `cancellation_price` it adds the opportunity cost of shares never filled. Its inputs are `trade_prices`, `benchmark_prices` and `trade_quantities`, plus `side` for buys or sells.

`portfolio_turnover` asks how much you traded: it takes `weights_before` and `weights_after` and gives the one-way traded fraction, half the sum of absolute weight changes. It says nothing about prices or the quality of execution.

In short, turnover measures the size of a rebalance, while `transaction_cost_analysis` measures what it cost to carry out the trades.

explain.text: `transaction_cost_analysis` (Transaction Cost Analysis) measures how much a set of fills cost relative to a benchmark. It computes per-trade slippage against an arrival or VWAP price, plus the quantity-weighted average slippage in basis points, with `side` set for buys or sells. If you also pass `decision_price`, it adds a delay-cost leg and an implementation shortfall measured against the price at the decision moment, following Perold (1988). Adding `unexecuted_quantity` and `cancellation_price` brings in the opportunity cost of shares never filled. It does not model commissions or fees.

when.text:
Use Transaction Cost Analysis (`transaction_cost_analysis`) when you want to see what trading actually cost against a benchmark:

- You have fills (executed prices, quantities) and an arrival or VWAP benchmark, and want slippage per trade plus a quantity-weighted average in basis points. Set `side` to +1 for buys and -1 for sells.
- You want to separate delay cost from execution slippage: add `decision_price`, the price when the investment decision was made, to get the delay-cost leg and an implementation shortfall figure.
- Part of the order never traded: pass `unexecuted_quantity` and `cancellation_price` together (with a single scalar `decision_price`) to add the opportunity cost of the unfilled shares.
- Keep in mind it has no explicit commission or fee leg.
- If your question is about how much a portfolio's weights changed between two points, `portfolio_turnover` is listed as the one-way traded fraction between two weight vectors.
